title: Form & Phenomenon / Goldstone Gallery / Melbourne Design Week 2026
paragraphs: Form & Phenomenon - A SOLO SHOW AT GOLDSTONE GALLERY, VIC Melbourne Design Week 2026 - Form & Phenomenon - A solo exhibition by Ilan El. In Form & Phenomenon , Ilan El investigates the decisive moment where structure surrenders to atmosphere. By distilling complex concepts to their skeletal essence, the works identify the liminal point where material meets the intangible.

The exhibition presents a series of luminous artworks and artifacts that command light as a primary medium to activate and transform spatial volume. Drawing on the emotional resonance of saturated colour fields and organic textures, these installations create an immersive environment designed to alter perception - an investigation into the restorative and emotive power of light.

Through the manipulation of directional radiance and hand-forged materiality, El challenges the boundary between the physical object and the sensory experience it commands. Each piece serves as a vital, luminous pulse that animates its environment, inviting the observer to engage with illumination as a living legacy.

This is a contemplative experience designed to be felt. Exhibition Dates 14 May – 14 June 2026 Goldstone Gallery 41 Derby Street, Collingwood Victoria 3066 Aether Bespoke Light Art | Series of 01 Aether is a singular exploration of chromatic bleed and spatial dissolution.

title: Now, You'll See / Goldstone Gallery
paragraphs: NOW YOU’LL SEE - A SOLO SHOW AT GOLDSTONE GALLERY, VIC Goldstone Gallery proudly presents - Now, you’ll see - A solo exhibition by Ilan El. Ilan El’s solo exhibition, Now, You’ll See , is both a compelling statement and an evocative invitation, urging viewers to engage not only with their eyes but with their full sensory awareness.

It marks the culmination of a long-held vision: light as a medium not just for seeing, but for feeling—a paradigm shift in perception. At the heart of Now, You’ll See is the radical idea that coloured light is more than mere illumination; it is a profound transformative force.

El’s works don’t aim to represent the world but rather to create an environment that directly affects the viewer. They invite total immersion, allowing light to intrinsically alter one’s internal state. The viewer becomes an integral part of the work, engaging with the shifting relationship among self, space, and perception.

The exhibition features a captivating progression through signature pieces, from the luminous elegance of ORA and its evolved version ORA 2.0 , to the expansive and meditative HORIZONS series. These works don’t simply light up their surroundings; they activate them.

title: Luminisim / The Horizon Series
paragraphs: Luminism - The Horizon Series An Expression of Luminism through Coloured Illumination. Mid-20th-century art historians originally introduced ‘Luminism’ to describe a 19th-century American painting style. “Luminist landscapes emphasise tranquillity and often depict calm, reflective water and soft, hazy majestic skies.

Characterised by the effects of light in landscapes, it stresses the horizontal and demonstrates the artist's control of structure, tone, and light.” HORIZONS is a series that redefines our perception of the world through the interplay of monochromatic photography and vibrant coloured illumination.

These works provoke deep emotional responses, foster heightened awareness, and offer a rich, dynamic, intimate experience. The series invites viewers on a contemplative and mindful journey by transforming familiar landscapes into vivid, illuminated scenes. The previously static photographs are animated through light, creating a harmonious blend of stillness and movement.

This unique synergy, enhanced by the hypnotic effect of transparent colour, induces meditative stillness and provides a transformative encounter with radiating coloured light. Each piece in the series is an opportunity to break free from the fast-paced world and fully engage with the intricate interplay of light and colour.

title: Ora / An Interactive Eclipse
paragraphs: Ora - An Interactive Eclipse The Intersection of Art, Design, and Psychology Presented at the 2020 Triennial , alongside the National Gallery of Victoria’s collection of early 20th-century design, Ora is an interactive light sculpture that sits at the intersection of psychological inquiry and environmental design.

It explores how our surroundings - specifically the quality and colour of light - profoundly shape human emotion and behaviour. As a mediator between light and darkness, Ora invites users into a tactile exploration of the RGB spectrum. Through three interactive spheres integrated into its face, the user becomes the artist, manually mixing Red, Green, and Blue light to sculpt a personalized atmosphere.

More than a luminaire, Ora is a tool for emotional expression, allowing the inhabitant to define the "aura" of their own space through the transformative power of transparent colour. Back to Light Art Home

title: Ora 2.0 / An Evolution of Colour Interplay
paragraphs: Ora 2.0 - DUAL GLOW The ORA 2.0 is an evolution of the original artwork ORA commissioned by the National Gallery of Victoria (NGV) and prominently displayed at the 2020 Triennial . This iteration builds upon the conceptual foundation of its predecessor, which featured a striking 1.2-meter diameter illuminated wall eclipse.

Drawing inspiration from the principles of Optical Art and the intricate ways humans perceive colour, the ORA 2.0 introduces a captivating dual illumination effect that sets it apart. The artwork embodies a sophisticated interplay of coloured illumination, where the dual inner and outer glow work in harmony to create a mesmerising visual experience.

The inner glow provides a concentrated, radiant core that draws the viewer's gaze, while the outer glow creates a subtle halo effect, enhancing the illusion of depth and movement. This duality is designed to engage viewers on both a sensory and emotional level, encouraging them to explore the nuances of colour and light as they interact with the space.

The ORA 2.0 is not merely an extension of the original piece but a reimagined creation that explores the boundaries of light as an artistic medium. It challenges the observer's perception by altering their sense of reality, making it an immersive experience. The subtle shifts in colour and light intensity evoke a sense of calmness and introspection, drawing viewers into a meditative state as they contemplate the relationship between light, colour, and space.

title: 39 Steps / Justin Art House Museum (JAHM)
paragraphs: 39 Steps / Justin art house museum An interactive lighting installation at JAHM's (Justin Art House Museum) central staircase. 39 steps is an installation that mediates between light and darkness through transparent colour. It is a rich immersion of play, experiment and the unpredictable.

Through its choreography of light shows, the central staircase at JAHM becomes an experience that transforms the perfunctory in a built environment into something random and unexpected. As people walk up and down the four flights of stairs, illuminated step rises are randomly triggered by motion sensors embedded in the architecture.

Each flight becomes a LED screen, where light shows illume and fade, race or trickle up and down and side to side. No ascent or descent is the same. As the subtle interplay of lights and pattern change the way people feel, they become animated, excited, playful and curious.

The desire to create an unpredictable experience of rhythm, spectrum and illumination demanded technical innovation. Transforming each step required 60 RGBW pixels, more than 2100 pixel chips, almost 6,500 thousand channels and 1500 lines of programming code to give the appearance of random variegated light shows. 39 steps is never static, and it will continue to evolve with more light shows, experimentation with screening content, and play of form.

title: Colours of Light / Solo Show at Linden Newart Gallery
paragraphs: Colours Of Light / Solo show, linden new art gallery The exhibition showcases a captivating collection of light works by artist and designer Ilan El. In a mesmerizing display of changing illuminations, El's creations delve into the depths of human experience by exploring the diverse range of emotions evoked by coloured light.

Each piece is meticulously crafted to unlock the potential of light, form, and colour to affect us psychologically and transform our perception of the world we inhabit. By pushing the boundaries of artistic expression, El's works invite viewers to embark on a profound journey of self-discovery, where the interplay of light and emotion unravels the complexities of the human soul.

title: Fragile / Melbourne Design Week 2023
paragraphs: Fragile / Melbourne Design Week 2023, Glowing Structures Gallery CANNONS OF HOPE - תותחים של תקוה The installation, Cannons of Hope, is a poignant expression of Ilan El's military service experiences as a soldier during the Gulf War and a testament to the strength of the human spirit in the face of conflict.

With a long history of military combat, Israeli soldiers, when presented with such violence, sing a famous song, “Flowers in the Barrel”, the heartfelt lyrics of which express a hopeful longing for a time of peace, where cannons are loaded with flowers instead of missiles.

Cannons of Hope creates a powerful metaphor for the resilience of the human spirit in the face of destruction. Using El’s highly acclaimed Cannon Vase range as its basis, this iteration of distorted vases, melted by overheating and deformed by stress, fire beams of light, casting a luminous cloud of hope and determination.

The use of glass as a medium highlights the delicate balance between control and unpredictability, characterising the creative process. Glass has its own will and yet is inherently fragile and vulnerable, creating a deeper layer of meaning to the work. The use of light expresses hope in darkness, where one state's experience relies on the juxtaposition of the other.

title: Reflections / Melbourne Design Week 2022
paragraphs: Reflections / Melbourne design week 2022, Glowing Structures Gallery How do we navigate the path out of crisis? How do we make good on the issues of climate change, pandemic isolation, economic and educational disparity, and the generational and systemic abuse of our environment? Reflections brings together a group of seven creatives from various cultures, ages, social demographics, and widely differing artistic practices.

It asks them to reflect on the problems humans face as a local, national and global community and how they can make good through the times they live as makers. ARTHUR DIMITRIOU + ILAN EL HEDY RITTERMAN GEORGE ANGELOVSKI YAN-HONG HUANG MOURNING BRIGHT HEATHER SCHWARZ Back to Light Art Home

title: Light + Life / Melbourne Design Week 2021
paragraphs: Light + Life / Melbourne Design Week 2020, Brightspace Gallery Of all environmental factors, light and colour are the ones with the swiftest and most significant impact on our well-being. Light+Life features immersive light-based installations, aiming to engage visitors in a multi-sensory journey.

A group of eight artists and designers harnessing design capabilities to produce light-based artworks, exploring how light affects us physically, mentally and emotionally Light+Life examines new ways of design thinking, employing the immaterial into shape and form, exploring paths to illuminate ideas.

The show displays various works, from meditative through scientific to aesthetic, weaving light through life narratives. ILAN EL | ALY INDERMUHLE | JAMES TAPSCOTT | VERONICA CAVEN ALDOUS | MARC PASCAL | JASMINE MORGAN RYAN | DANI STORM RESONANCE: The Intersection of Light, Life, and Physiology RESONANCE is an immersive art installation that explores the profound connection between the human body and the physics of light.

Created for Melbourne Design Week, this project by Ilan El transforms clinical data into an emotive, sensory experience, bridging the gap between medical science and artistic expression. The Vision While medical imaging traditionally provides a cold, analytical view of our interior selves, RESONANCE seeks to humanise this data.

title: SOL / Two suns, one light
paragraphs: SOL / A story of two suns SOL is a celebration of the majestic Australian Sun. Sources of light as an architectural device have long held a fascination for contemplation and divine inspiration. The piece references Bernini’s baroque theatricality by thrusting golden rays into centre stage in this bespoke luminary.

The engraved front face is an emblematic dotted sun, influenced by graphic indigenous representations. SOL stimulates the senses, and elevates the soul, using tension, texture and naturalism. Back to Light Art Home

title: Light Matter / mental functions and behaviour of light through ritual
paragraphs: Light Matter / GLOBELIGHT, 2014 In central, western and southern parts of Australia, a black stone was revered as rare and much prized by the people of the land for its curative powers. Often with various purposes, they were looked upon as objects of magic and mystery, most commonly applied in sorcery or medical use.

Commonly known as obsidian, the artefact is extraordinarily dark in colour, extremely brittle and highly reflective. They were gathered with respect for ceremonial and healing purposes, such as native psychotherapy. Rituals of now still practice in the transmission of messages.

An obsidian pendulum tied to an electrical cord suspended from a pivot can demonstrate the same rotation of Earth, the natural physics of gravity, period of oscillation, inertia, and even air drag - but all conclude toward an equilibrium position. Conversely, a thurible with burning incense purifies holy spaces and beckons the divine creator.

Fundamentally, this revelation of ceremony gives evidence to neurological patterns of the right hemisphere as an ancient engraving of ghost lines that appear before time has stopped. This unification of opposites fields of knowledge and the polarised worldview of ILAN EL and GEORGE ANGELOVSKI profanely harmonises the study of mental functions and behaviour of light through ritual. 535 x 610mm fibre-based photographic paper. 590 x 710mm framed.

title: Tree Change - A New Christmas Tree for the City of Melbourne
paragraphs: Tree CHANGE - Melbourne’s New Christmas tree A Living Canvas: Uniting Melbourne Through the Christmas Tree Christmas embodies the power of togetherness – expressed through song, acts of kindness, and the cherished moments of gathering with family and friends for festive celebrations and gift-giving.

It was this very essence of unity that inspired our redesign of the city square Christmas tree. We envisioned a tree that acts as a focal point, drawing together individuals from all walks of life and infusing the city with the spirit of the season. Mindful of the project’s brief and prioritizing sustainability, longevity, and feasibility, our proposal reimagines the existing structure as a dynamic canvas using LED panels.

This transformation allows the tree to become a powerful vehicle for delivering messages – messages of creation, welcome, and shared joy. This digital canvas becomes a platform for the people. It can display any digital creation, fostering community expression, from the artwork of local residents to the imaginative drawings of preschoolers.

We recognize the transformative potential of LED technology and believe this is an exceptional opportunity for Melbourne to lead the way globally. The City of Melbourne can curate content from artists, experts, and students, inviting them to share their unique Christmas messages.
